title: observability: token/KV logging & metrics + dashboard + alert tuning
author: Aditi Rao
description: Context: debugging a recent regression where per-request cost and tail latency increased for a small set of high-throughput routes was difficult due to lack of token-level visibility and KV-cache observability. This PR adds token-level metrics and structured logging to correlate tokens -> KV cache hits/misses -> per-token latency and implicit cost estimates, plus Grafana dashboards and tuned alerts. Motivation: enable fast incident triage and automated regression detection for cost/latency changes without requiring sampling-heavy traces. What this PR does: 1) adds Prometheus metrics for token latency, token cost estimate (cents/token), KV cache hit/miss counters and ratios, per-model and per-route labels; 2) augments request tracing (OTel) to include token-level spans and KV cache span events so traces can be correlated with metrics; 3) structured logs for token events (token_index, model, route, kv_hit, token_latency_ms, estimated_cost_cents) exported to existing logging pipeline; 4) new Grafana dashboard (Token-Level Cost & KV Metrics) with P50/P95/P99 token latency, token-cost histogram, KV hit heatmap, per-route breakdowns, and example alert query links; 5) tuned alerts: reduced noisy alerting by changing thresholds and adding anomaly-detection windows for KV hit rate drops and token-P95 regressions; 6) tests: unit tests for metric labeling and a small e2e that validates metric emission in a local integration harness; 7) docs: updated observability docs with usage examples and dashboard screenshots. Backwards compatibility: metrics and logs opt-in via feature flag "observability.token_level_enabled" (default enabled for new clusters), and telemetry schema additions are additive. Checklist: - [x] metric instrumentation added and unit tested - [x] OTel spans and log format documented - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON included - [x] Alert rules tuned with test queries - [x] e2e smoke to verify no regressions in core request path Notes: kept cardinality low by limiting label set to {model, route, customer_tier} and using hash buckets for rarely-used route ids. Follow-ups planned: automated regression detection job that scans token-cost deltas per-release (ENG-3508).

review_conversation: Carlos Mendes (reviewer): Left high level comments: prefer low-cardinality labels; please ensure model & route are limited to known enums. Also request to document the hash-bucketing approach.
Aditi Rao (author): Reply: implemented label whitelist and hash-bucketing for route ids in token_metrics.go; added documentation section 'label-cardinality' with examples.

Sophie Li (reviewer): Comment: alert for KV hit-rate drop was firing too often in canary; suggest adding a 10m anomaly window and require sustained drop >10% for 5m. Also asked for trimmed dashboard to remove redundant panels.

Aditi Rao (author): Reply: tuned alert to use increase() with a 5m sustained window and added optional suppression via silence during deploys; removed duplicate panels and consolidated into 'KV hit heatmap'.
Raj Patel (reviewer): Approve after minor nits addressed: rename metric redwood_inference_token_latency_seconds -> redwood_inference_token_processing_duration_seconds for clarity.
